# DoW Manual 5000.103 — Cyber Developmental Test and Evaluation

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering — the document's own title block names the "Department of War," the current name of record for the U.S. Department of Defense as of this issuance. |
| **Kind** | Policy manual (acquisition directive series) |
| **Status** | Effective 2026-02-25; approved 2026-02-19 by Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. |
| **Where to get it** | Public: Directives Division website, esd.whs.mil/DD/ (per the document's own releasability statement). Public copy, confirmed anonymously off-network on 2026-10-26: `https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/5000103m.PDF` (opens in an ordinary browser; scripted clients get HTTP 403) |
| **Binds whom** | DoW/DoD acquisition programs — "implements policy, assigns responsibilities, and prescribes procedures for cyber developmental test and evaluation (DT&E)" (Purpose statement, verbatim). |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** The directive-level policy manual underneath the
Cyber DT&E Guidebook (below); useful as the binding-policy end of a policy/guidebook pair, a structure
NASA uses too (NPR vs. handbook) (our reading).

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.** Coordinates its cyber DT&E processes with "the
Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer (CDAO)" and references the "DoD Data, Analytics, and
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption Strategy and the DoD Responsible AI Toolkit" (§ on coordination
responsibilities, paraphrase/partial quote). A text search of the public PDF finds "Artificial Intelligence"
named 5 times and "Machine Learning" twice — AI is a named coordination point, not a central topic of
this manual.

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** No NASA policy document is a direct analogue; compares structurally to
`../documents/NPR_7150.2D.md` as the binding-directive half of a policy/handbook pair (our reading).
